title: Fewer Americans Have a Side Hustle in 2025 - Bankrate
summary: Survey press release: a quarter of US adults have a side hustle, median income is a few hundred dollars a month, mostly spent on living costs or discretionary purchases.

assertions.quote: Side hustlers earn an average of $885 per month, but the median is just $200 per month.

verdicts.note: Survey data consistently show heavily right-skewed side-hustle earnings with a low median.

For MLM specifically the typical participant earns far less than a few hundred a month: the vast majority received $1,000 or less per year (under $84/month) before expenses; MLM is one side-hustle type, so this narrows rather than tests the general claim.

assertions.quote: More than a third of side hustlers (35%) say they use at least some of the extra income to pay for regular living expenses

verdicts.note: Bankrate finds only a minority save any of it; consistent with other surveys.

assertions.quote: A strong job market and a cooling inflation rate are the biggest reasons why fewer people are side hustling this year

verdicts.note: Plausible and consistent with the survey trend, but it is an analyst's interpretation rather than a tested relationship.

assertions.quote: The average side hustler could earn enough to pay off the average credit card balance ($6,371, according to TransUnion) in about seven months.

verdicts.note: Uses the mean; at the median side-hustle income it would take nearly three years.
The figure uses mean side-hustle income; at the median it would take years, not months.

assertions.quote: Younger generations are more likely to have side hustles compared to older generations

verdicts.note: Consistent across several independent side-hustle surveys.

assertions.quote: about 3 in 10 side hustlers (29%) think they will always need a side hustle to make ends meet
